title: Subcommand help: every command prints its own usage and exits 0 on --help or -h
lead: *Proposed.* `ork SUB --help` and `ork SUB -h` print that subcommand's usage on stdout and exit 0, for every command in `ork help`. A test walks the command table so a new command cannot skip it. What the subcommand help prints, and what `ork help SUB` does, are open: see `Open owner questions`.
findings_note: Owner 2026-11-04: ork retry --help prints 'ork: retry: flag: help requested' and 'Run ork help for usage.' (exit 2). Verified 2026-11-04 for every command in ork help: none prints its own usage on --help or -h; ork help SUB prints the whole usage.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** new usage wording for any command; `--json` help output; the TUI's help; `ork daemon run`'s own usage text (it is the daemon's entry point, `cmd/ork/main.go:125-128`), except that `--help` there also exits 0.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Verified on 2026-11-04 with `~/bin/ork` (built 2026-11-04 13:39 from main), read-only, for every command `ork help` lists, with both `--help` and `-h`. Every one exits 2 and prints no usage:

- Commands that parse flags first print "ork: CMD: flag: help requested" then "Run 'ork help' for usage.": `run`, `wave suggest`, `wave start`, `approve`, `check`, `fix`, `stop`, `new`, `note`, `file`, `adj answer`, `adj ask`, `answer`, `dismiss`, `retry`, `status`, `projects list|add|rm|pin|unpin|set`, `settings show|set`, `vendor` (as `vendor list`), `vendor list|out|back`, `roles print`, `roles matrix`, `daemon stop|restart`, `doctor`.
- Group commands take `--help` as an unknown subcommand: `wave` ("wave needs suggest or start"), `adj` ("adj: unknown command \"--help\""), `projects` ("unknown projects command \"--help\""), `settings`, `roles` ("roles needs the subcommand print or matrix"), `daemon` ("daemon needs stop or restart [--force]").
- `ork daemon run --help` prints "ork: usage: ork daemon run" and exits 2 (`cmd/ork/main.go:125-128`).
- `ork help retry` prints the whole usage (exit 0), not retry's.
- Already right: only `ork help`, `ork --help` and `ork -h` (the whole usage, exit 0; `TestHelp`, `internal/cli/cli_test.go:540`; `TestHelpReachesTheCommandLine`, `cmd/ork/main_test.go:184`).

The code: every command builds a `flag.FlagSet` and calls `parse` (`internal/cli/cli.go:217-231`), which sets output to `io.Discard` and returns `flag.ErrHelp` for `-h` or `--help`. Each command then reports it as a usage error through `o.usage` (`cli.go:205-207`), and `fail` adds "Run 'ork help' for usage." (`cli.go:193-203`). Help is handled only as the first word (`internal/cli/cli.go:241-243`, in App.Run). The usage is one text, `usageTemplate` (`cli.go:44` on), with one block per command that starts at a line `  ork CMD ...` and continues on lines indented 30 columns. `TestLaunchUsageFitsEightyColumns` (`internal/cli/run_test.go:627`) keeps it at 80 columns.

Owner evidence, 2026-11-04: the orchestrator ran `ork retry --help` to learn the retry form and got the error above.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/cli/cli.go:205-243` (`usage`, `parse`, `App.Run`: handle `flag.ErrHelp` in one place, and `help SUB`).
- `internal/cli/help.go` (new; `// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later`): `commandUsage(words []string) (string, bool)`, which cuts the matching blocks out of `usageText`.
- `cmd/ork/main.go:85-91` and `:125-128` (`daemon run --help`).
- `internal/cli/help_test.go` (new) and `internal/cli/cli_test.go:540` (`TestHelp`), `:517` (`TestUsageErrorsExitTwo` stays green).
- `docs/design.md:1189` (CLI: one sentence on `--help`) and `docs/guide.md` if it describes `ork help`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
In `internal/cli/help_test.go`:

- `TestEveryCommandPrintsItsOwnHelp`: build the command table from `usageText` (every line that starts with `  ork `; the command words up to the first argument in capitals or the first `[`). For each command, and for each of `--help` and `-h`, `run(t, noDaemon(t), words..., flag)` exits 0, writes nothing to stderr, and prints on stdout the block for that command (its first line starts with `ork WORDS`) and no other command's block. The daemon is never called (`App.Call` fails the test). Fails first: exit 2 with "flag: help requested".
- `TestGroupHelpListsItsSubcommands`: `ork projects --help` prints every `ork projects ...` block and nothing else; the same for `wave`, `adj`, `settings`, `vendor`, `roles`, `daemon`. Fails first: exit 2.
- `TestHelpSubcommand` (Q2 option 1): `ork help retry` prints only the retry block, exit 0; `ork help nosuch` exits 2 with "unknown command". Fails first: the whole usage.
- `TestHelpFlagAfterArgumentsStillHelps`: `ork retry RUN --help` prints retry's usage and does not call the daemon. Fails first: exit 2.
- `TestCommandTableMatchesTheDispatcher`: every command word in the table is dispatched by `App.Run` (a command that `App.Run` does not know fails the test), so the table and the switch stay in step. Fails first: compiles only once `commandUsage` exists.

In `cmd/ork/main_test.go`:

- `TestDaemonRunHelpExitsZero`: `ork daemon run --help` exits 0 and prints its usage line on stdout without starting the daemon. Fails first: exit 2 on stderr.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Tests first. Confirm each fails for the reason given.
2. `commandUsage` returns the blocks of `usageText` whose first line's command words start with the given words. A group returns all of its blocks.
3. In `usage` (`cli.go:205`), or in one wrapper every command uses: when the error is `flag.ErrHelp`, print `commandUsage(command words)` to stdout and return `ExitOK`. Group dispatchers treat a first argument of `--help` or `-h` the same way.
4. `App.Run`: `help` with arguments prints `commandUsage(args)` (Q2).
5. `cmd/ork/main.go`: `daemon run --help` or `-h` prints `usage: ork daemon run` on stdout and exits 0.
6. Do not reword any usage line. Keep `TestLaunchUsageFitsEightyColumns` green.
7. Update `docs/design.md` (CLI) in the same diff.

Owner decisions (2026-11-11): How should this slice's Check run its focused tests and mutation step? -> orchestrator: keep `go -C WORKTREE test -count=1 ./internal/cli ./cmd/ork -run 'Help|Usage'` and the mutation step as written, and assign both to the orchestrator to run..

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go -C WORKTREE test -count=1 ./internal/cli ./cmd/ork -run 'Help|Usage'`: all pass.
- `go -C WORKTREE test -race -count=1 ./...`, `go -C WORKTREE vet ./...`, `gofmt -l WORKTREE` (empty), `slicer check`, `adj lint`.
- Mutation: skip the `flag.ErrHelp` branch for one command; `TestEveryCommandPrintsItsOwnHelp` goes red for that command.
- [HUMAN CHECK] `ork retry --help`, `ork projects -h` and `ork help wave` in a terminal print the expected blocks and exit 0.

sections.heading: Open owner questions
sections.body:
UI slice by rule u10 (`internal/cli` output), so it gets a UI pass.

Question: What should a subcommand's help print?
Options:
1. usage-block: the command's block cut from the one usage text, so there is a single source
2. flag-defaults: a usage line plus each flag and its default from the FlagSet
3. full-usage: the whole ork help text, exit 0
Recommend: 1 - one source keeps help and ork help in step, and the blocks already document every flag

Question: What should ork help SUB print?
Options:
1. sub-only: the same blocks as ork SUB --help, and an unknown SUB is a usage error
2. full: the whole usage, as today
Recommend: 1 - it is what the orchestrator tried first, and it costs one line in App.Run
